Abel-shittim
AY-bel-shit-TEEM
proper noun
Hebrew Abel hash-Shittim, “meadow of the acacias,” the last encampment of Israel in the plains of Moab before the crossing of Jordan.

Biblical Definition

Abel-shittim, called also simply Shittim, was the last camp of Israel in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan over against Jericho, before the nation passed over into the promised land. From Beth-jeshimoth unto Abel-shittim the tents of the tribes were spread along the river (Num 33:49). It was a place of both temptation and triumph. Here Israel, at the very border of the inheritance, was drawn into whoredom with the daughters of Moab and bowed down to Baal-peor, and the plague consumed twenty and four thousand until Phinehas rose up and turned away the wrath of God (Num 25:1). Here too the second numbering of the people was taken, and from here Joshua sent the two spies into Jericho. The prophet Micah bids Israel remember the way from Shittim unto Gilgal, that they may know the righteousness of the LORD (Mic 6:5). The dictionary holds up Abel-shittim as the meadow where the flesh was proved at the threshold of promise. These things were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come (1Co 10:11); the believer nearest his rest is not beyond the reach of temptation, and must watch unto prayer until Jordan is crossed indeed.

Webster 1828 Definition

Israel’s last camp in the plains of Moab before crossing Jordan, the scene of the sin of Baal-peor.

expand to see more

ABEL-SHITTIM, the “meadow of the acacias” in the plains of Moab over against Jericho.

It was the final encampment of Israel before the crossing of the Jordan.

Here the people sinned with Moab and bowed to Baal-peor, and a plague fell.

Here Phinehas stayed the plague, and the second census of Israel was taken.

From Shittim Joshua sent spies to Jericho, and from Shittim the nation went over.

Key Scripture

Num 33:49 — "And they pitched by Jordan, from Bethjesimoth even unto Abelshittim in the plains of Moab."

Num 25:1 — "And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab."

Mic 6:5 — "O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the LORD."

1Co 10:11 — "Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come."

Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it warns that the flesh is proved even at the border of promise.

expand to see more

Abel-shittim has drawn no redefinition from the present age, for the world has little use for a meadow remembered chiefly for a plague of judgment. The dictionary records the place that the reader may know the geography of Israel’s last camp, and may not forget what was done there.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the watchfulness of the saint at the threshold of his rest. Israel sinned grievously when the inheritance was almost in hand, and the same temper of presumption besets the believer who counts himself past danger. Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall; the meadow of the acacias is a standing warning that nearness to promise is no charter for carelessness of soul.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “meadow of the acacias,” the name marks Israel’s last camp in Moab.

expand to see more

Abel-shittim — Hebrew Abel hash-Shittim, “meadow of the acacias.”

Abel signifies a meadow or grassy place; shittim, the acacia trees.

It lay in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, over against Jericho.

It was the last encampment of Israel before the crossing of the river.

It was the scene of the sin of Baal-peor and the plague that followed.

Usage

"Like Israel at Abel-shittim, the saint nearest his rest is not beyond the reach of temptation."

"Remember the way from Shittim unto Gilgal, that you may know the righteousness of the LORD."

"These things were written for our admonition, that we sin not at the border of promise."
